items.title: Approval is not the lock
items.body:
`assertEditable` throws only when `isPayrollCycleEditable(status)` is false, and that helper returns false only for LOCKED, PROCESSED and CLOSED. An APPROVED cycle is still editable, so the adjustment's payroll item can be added.

- *Approved means frozen*: the code protects a cycle from LOCKED onwards, not from approval.
- *OPEN only*: every state before LOCKED is editable.
- *Moves the cycle back*: `assertEditable` only reads the cycle; it never changes its status.

items.title: Approved unpaid days at 1/22 of salary
items.body:
For each employment, `create` finds time-off requests of type UNPAID with status APPROVED that overlap the period, and sums their `days`: only the approved 3. The deduction is `-Math.round((salary / 22) * unpaidDays)` = -Math.round(20000 * 3) = -60000. The 22 is an assumed number of working days per month.

- *-100000* also counts the REQUESTED 2 days, which the status filter excludes.
- *-40000* uses a 33-day month; the code divides by 22.
- *No deduction until APPROVED*: the deduction item is written when the cycle is created, at OPEN.

items.title: The balance guard runs before the write
items.body:
For an approved VACATION request, `review` ensures a balance exists, computes `usedAfter = usedDays + days` = 13 + 3 = 16, and throws "Approving this request would exceed the worker's vacation balance." because 16 > 15. Nothing is written.

- *Capped at 15*: there is no capping; the approval is refused.
- *16 days used*: the check throws before the increment.
- *Only 2 days could be requested*: `create` never checks the balance; the limit applies at approval.

items.title: Basis points: divide by 10,000
items.body:
The EMPLOYER_COST item is `Math.round((salaryAmountMinor * employerCostRateBps) / 10000)`. With 650000 and 1600 that is 650000 * 1600 / 10000 = 104000 minor units, GBP 1,040.00. 1600 bps means 16%.

- *10400* divides by 100,000, a factor of ten too many.
- *1040000* divides by 1,000 instead of 10,000.
- *650000* would be a 100% rate; employer cost is a separate, smaller item.

items.title: No silent currency mixing
items.body:
`addMoney` takes the first item's currency, then reduces the rest. Before adding each one it compares currencies; the USD item differs from GBP, so it throws "Cannot add money across currencies without an FX conversion."

- *Treated as GBP*: the comparison prevents exactly that.
- *Skipped silently*: the code throws rather than skipping.
- *Last currency wins*: the total uses the first item's currency, and here it never gets that far.

excerpts.quote: throw new Error("Cannot add money across currencies without an FX conversion.");

items.title: The fee is 7% of the signed subtotal
items.body:
`createFromPayroll` sums every item's `amountMinor`, deductions included: 500000 + 70000 - 20000 = 550000. The fee is `Math.round(550000 * 0.07)` = 38500. The total is 588500.

- *609900* drops the deduction: 570000 plus a 39900 fee.
- *631300* adds the deduction as if it were positive: 590000 plus a 41300 fee.
- *585000* takes the fee on base pay alone (35000) instead of on the subtotal.

items.title: The pure rules: state maps, money and country profiles
items.body:
`packages/domain/src/states.ts` holds one transition map per workflow (hire requests, payroll cycles, time off, expenses) and a shared `assertTransition`. Write each map out as a diagram and note the terminal states. Then search the services for every place a status is written, and check which ones go through `assertTransition` and which use their own inline check.

`packages/domain/src/money.ts` defines `money()` and `addMoney()`. Note what each rejects and what an empty list returns.

`packages/domain/src/country-profile.ts` lists the three supported countries with their default currency, PTO days and employer cost rate in basis points (1 bps = 0.01%). `HiringService.create` uses the profile to validate a hire's salary currency; read the condition it checks.

The isPayrollCycleEditable helper sits next to the payroll map. Read its list carefully, because later features ask it whether they may still change a cycle.

excerpts.quote: Instead of allowing any code to set any status string, the app defines allowed transitions in one place.

readMore.why: Tests for allowed and rejected transitions.

items.title: Each payroll state has one successor
items.body:
`payrollCycleTransitions` is a straight line: OPEN, COLLECTING_INPUTS, INTERNAL_REVIEW, CLIENT_REVIEW, APPROVED, LOCKED, PROCESSED, CLOSED. APPROVED lists only LOCKED, so `assertTransition` throws for CLOSED before `advance` reaches any other guard.

- *CLOSED is terminal, so allowed*: terminal means nothing leaves CLOSED; it does not let you jump into it.
- *Editability instead*: the transition check runs first and throws.
- *Needs an invoice*: `advance` never looks at invoices.

items.title: From employment to invoice: the payroll pipeline
items.body:
`PayrollService.create` builds a cycle from ACTIVE employment records for one organization and country. Inside one transaction it writes, per employment: a base-pay item, an employer-cost item, an optional unpaid-leave deduction, and reimbursement items for approved expenses. For each item, write down the formula and the filter on the records it reads (status, type, dates, currency).

`PayrollService.advance` moves a cycle along the payroll map with extra guards, and `assertEditable` is what adjustments and expenses call before touching a cycle.

`InvoicesService.createFromPayroll` turns a cycle into an invoice: read its three refusals in order, how the currency is chosen, and how subtotal, fee and total are computed from the items.

For time off, `TimeOffService.review` updates a vacation balance on approval; note where its balance check sits relative to its transaction, and where `days` comes from in `create`.

readMore.why: Invoice generation from an approved cycle.

items.title: An inline check instead of the transition map
items.body:
`approveForWorker` checks `["SUBMITTED", "INTERNAL_REVIEW"].includes(before.status)` instead of calling `assertTransition`, then sets the request to WORKER_ONBOARDING and creates the worker and employment. The map would require SUBMITTED, INTERNAL_REVIEW, READY_FOR_WORKER, then WORKER_ONBOARDING; the inline check skips that.

- *Needs READY_FOR_WORKER*: the map says so, but this method does not consult the map.
- *INTERNAL_REVIEW only*: SUBMITTED is in the allowed list too.
- *Moves to READY_FOR_WORKER*: the status written is WORKER_ONBOARDING.

items.title: The country fixes the salary currency
items.body:
After checking that the organization is APPROVED, `create` loads the country profile and throws when `country.defaultCurrency !== dto.salaryCurrency`. GB's default is GBP, so a USD salary is refused with "Salary currency for GB must be GBP."

- *Converted*: there is no conversion; the request is refused.
- *Checked later*: the check is in `create`, before the request is stored.
- *Only US may use USD*: true in effect, but the refusal is about GB requiring GBP, not a USD rule.

items.title: Start here: GlobalWork, a NestJS employer-of-record monorepo
items.body:
GlobalWork is a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo: a NestJS API (`apps/api`), a Next.js web app, a background worker, and shared packages, notably `packages/domain` (pure rules: state machines, money, country profiles) and `packages/database` (Prisma).

The guides come in two sets:

1. `docs/code-walkthroughs/`: one file per important source file, read line by line. Start with 03 (domain states), 05 (money), 11 (hiring), 14 (payroll) and 15 (invoices).
2. `docs/features/`: one file per feature with a plan and a build journal. The payroll-related ones are 04 (time off), 12 (payroll locking), 13 (adjustments), 33 (balances) and 34 (expenses into payroll).

The walkthroughs quote line numbers from an earlier version of some files, so locate code by function name. The quizzes give concrete inputs; compute the answers from the current code.

excerpts.quote: This directory is a guided tour of the highest-value files in the GlobalWork codebase.
Payroll is where business correctness starts to feel real.

readMore.why: Every workflow state machine in one file.

items.title: The client says how many days
items.body:
`TimeOffService.create` checks only that `endDate` is not before `startDate`, then stores `days: dto.days` unchanged. The DTO's only rule is `@Min(0.5)`. A Monday-to-Friday request with `days: 1` is saved as one day (the feature 33 notes call this out).

- *5 days computed*: nothing derives days from the dates.
- *A 400 mismatch*: no comparison between days and dates exists.
- *7 days*: the server never counts calendar days either.

items.title: Expenses are matched on currency
items.body:
`create` loads expenses that are APPROVED_FOR_PAYROLL, have no `payrollCycleId`, and whose `currency` equals the employment's `salaryCurrency`. The GBP expense matches: it becomes an EXPENSE_REIMBURSEMENT item and its `payrollCycleId` is set. The EUR one is not loaded, so it stays approved and unattached.

- *Converted at a stored rate*: there is no FX anywhere in this service.
- *Only through attach-payroll*: that endpoint exists too, but cycle creation also picks up matching expenses.
- *The call fails*: the EUR expense is filtered out before any sum, so nothing mixes currencies.

items.title: Invoices wait for an approved cycle
items.body:
`createFromPayroll` first refuses a cycle that already has an invoice, then refuses any status outside APPROVED, LOCKED, PROCESSED and CLOSED. CLIENT_REVIEW is outside that list, so it throws "Payroll must be approved before an invoice can be generated."

- *Created at review*: review comes before approval in the payroll map, and the list does not include it.
- *Already has an invoice*: that is the first check, and this cycle has none.
- *A DRAFT invoice*: the method has no draft mode; it creates or it throws.
